tagline: One canyon, two outlets, and a flume hung on a cliff.
intro: From Whitewater on the Gunnison, CO 141 turns into Unaweep Canyon and runs through it to Gateway. Past Gateway it follows the Dolores, then the San Miguel by way of Uravan and Naturita, and CO 145 carries it on to Placerville. The canyon cuts through the red sandstone of the Uncompahgre Plateau down to Precambrian rock, under cliffs a thousand feet high.
Two creeks drain the one canyon in opposite directions. The Hayden Survey wondered at that in the 19th century, and the question of what carved it is still argued.

moments.title: Unaweep Divide
moments.text: Near mile marker 135 the road crosses the Unaweep Divide at 7,048 feet, a rise so slight it is hardly noticed, with East Creek draining one way and West Creek the other.

moments.title: Hanging Flume
moments.text: About two dozen workers, most of them Asian immigrants, hung on ropes to fix this flume to the cliff above the Dolores, and it ran three years before the mine closed.

moments.title: Uravan
moments.text: Named for uranium and vanadium, the company town once kept over 800 people, a school and a pool beside the San Miguel, and none of its buildings remain.

practical: Some sections have no fuel or cell service, with long intervals between service stops.
